gw_issue.gone.android_ppp: Android 12 and later can’t create PPTP and L2TP connections — use IKEv2.
gw_issue.gone.androidtv: Android TV has no built-in VPN.
gw_issue.gone.apple_pptp: Apple removed PPTP from iOS and macOS in 2016 (iOS 10, macOS 10.12) — use IKEv2.
gw_issue.gone.ios_sstp: iOS has no built-in SSTP — use IKEv2.
gw_issue.gone.macos_sstp: macOS has no built-in SSTP — use IKEv2.
gw_issue.howto.awg_paste: In {app}: “+” → “Insert” (pastes the key from the clipboard) → “Continue”, then “Connect”.
gw_issue.howto.awg_paste_neutral: In {app}: tap “+”, insert the key from the clipboard and connect.
gw_issue.howto.router_check: Turn the connection on and check that websites open.
gw_issue.howto.ui_keenetic: the Keenetic web interface: Internet → Other connections → WireGuard → “Import from a file”
gw_issue.howto.vless_paste: In {app}: tap “+” and import the link from the clipboard (in v2rayN — Ctrl+V in the server list), then connect.
gw_issue.howto.vless_scan: In {app}, tap “+” and scan the QR code.
gw_issue.howto.wg_name: Name the connection, for example gKP-wg, and turn it on.
gw_issue.howto.wg_paste_macos: In WireGuard: “Add Empty Tunnel…”, clear the text in the window, paste the copied text and save.
gw_issue.howto.wg_paste_windows: In WireGuard: “Add Tunnel” → “Add empty tunnel…”, clear the text in the window, paste the copied text and save.
gw_issue.howto.wg_scan_android: In WireGuard, tap “+” → “Scan from QR code”.
gw_issue.howto.wg_scan_ios: In WireGuard, tap “+” → “Create from QR code”.
gw_issue.install.builtin: Built into the system — no app needed.
gw_issue.install.fakes: The store has fakes with a similar name — install only by this link
gw_issue.install.none: {proto} on {os} — there is no app: choose another protocol or system.
gw_issue.ios.install: Settings → “Profile Downloaded” → “Install” (the iPhone asks for the passcode).
gw_issue.ios_move.agent: Open the file on the iPhone or iPad; saved it on another device? Move it there (AirDrop from a Mac or “Files” → iCloud Drive).
gw_issue.ios_move.bot: Open the file on the iPhone or iPad; Telegram on another device? Forward the file to your “Saved Messages” (or AirDrop it from a Mac).
gw_issue.ios_move.menu: Move the file to the iPhone or iPad (AirDrop from a Mac or “Files” → iCloud Drive) and open it.
gw_issue.ios_move.page: Open the file on the iPhone or iPad; downloaded it on another device? Move it there (AirDrop from a Mac or “Files” → iCloud Drive).
gw_issue.mac.install: Double-click the file → System Settings → General → Device Management (macOS 13–14: Privacy and Security → Profiles) → under “Downloaded”, double-click the profile → “Install”.
gw_issue.mac.turn_on: System Settings → VPN → “{name}” — turn it on.
gw_issue.note.androidtv: A TV has no camera: paste the vpn:// link from the clipboard or load the .conf file.
gw_issue.note.ios: AmneziaVPN is hidden in the Russian App Store — use AmneziaWG or DefaultVPN.
gw_issue.note.keenetic: AmneziaWG 3.1 — only from KeeneticOS 5.2 Alpha 11 (preview channel); on firmware before 5.1.1 — line 1.0 or WireGuard.
gw_issue.note.mikrotik: RouterOS has no AmneziaWG — only in a container; WireGuard is simpler.
gw_issue.note.openwrt: OpenWrt has no official AmneziaWG packages — only community builds.
gw_issue.note.ppp_routers: These routers usually have only L2TP and PPTP.
gw_issue.note.tplink: Look for a “VPN client” section in the router menu; if there is none, the router won’t work. TP-Link usually has only L2TP and PPTP.
gw_issue.offer.awg_tv: AmneziaVPN: easiest to paste the vpn:// link from the clipboard; AmneziaWG — the .conf file
gw_issue.offer.awg_vpn: AmneziaVPN: vpn:// link or QR; AmneziaWG: .conf file or QR
gw_issue.offer.awg_vpn_qr: AmneziaVPN: vpn:// link or QR; AmneziaWG: .conf file or QR
gw_issue.offer.hy2: Hysteria2 (UDP): hysteria2:// link or QR — v2RayTun, Hiddify, Karing, v2rayN
gw_issue.offer.ikev2_android: built-in IKEv2 client — Android 12 or later
gw_issue.offer.keenetic_awg2: KeeneticOS 5.1.1 or later: “Import from a file”
gw_issue.offer.l2tp_old_models: older models have only L2TP without IPsec
gw_issue.offer.ocserv_cisco: Cisco Secure Client: address, login and password
gw_issue.offer.ocserv_gui: OpenConnect GUI or Cisco Secure Client
gw_issue.offer.ocserv_linux: openconnect command with the certificate fingerprint
gw_issue.offer.openvpn_asus: the router’s VPN client: import the .ovpn file
gw_issue.offer.openvpn_windows: OpenVPN Connect or OpenVPN GUI: .ovpn file
gw_issue.offer.pptp_if_on: only if the protocol is on
gw_issue.offer.vless_android: v2RayTun, Hiddify, v2rayNG or NekoBox: vless:// link or QR
gw_issue.offer.vless_any: any VLESS client (Hiddify, v2RayTun, v2rayN): vless:// link
gw_issue.offer.vless_ios: Streisand or Hiddify: vless:// link or QR
gw_issue.offer.vless_macos: Hiddify, Streisand or v2rayN: vless:// link
gw_issue.offer.vless_tv: v2RayTun or Hiddify: paste the vless:// link from the clipboard
gw_issue.ovpn_move.agent: Move the .ovpn file to {target} (for example, via Telegram “Saved Messages”) and open it in OpenVPN Connect.
gw_issue.ovpn_move.bot: Forward the .ovpn file to yourself on {target} — for example, to Telegram “Saved Messages” — and open it in OpenVPN Connect.
gw_issue.ovpn_move.menu: Move the .ovpn file to {target} (to a phone — for example, via Telegram “Saved Messages”) and open it in OpenVPN Connect.
gw_issue.ovpn_move.page: Downloaded it somewhere other than {target}? Move the .ovpn file there (for example, via Telegram “Saved Messages”). Open it in OpenVPN Connect.
gw_issue.plain_off_note: This router usually supports L2TP only without IPsec, and it is off on the server — {plain_on}.
gw_issue.plain_on.agent: turn on L2TP without encryption on the server: ask the agent (inbound_option l2tp plain on) or use the SSH menu gokaskad → {path}
gw_issue.plain_on.bot: turn on L2TP without encryption on the server: SSH menu gokaskad → 17 → 1 → 5 → 2 or the web panel, “Protocols” → L2TP/IPsec
gw_issue.plain_on.menu: turn on L2TP without encryption on the server: gokaskad → {path}
gw_issue.plain_on.page: ask whoever sent you the link to turn on L2TP without encryption on the server
gw_issue.plain_on.panel: turn on L2TP without encryption on the server: “Protocols” → L2TP/IPsec → “L2TP without encryption”
gw_issue.ppp_fields: server address, username (the device login) and password

gw_issue.qr.page: Point the camera at the QR code below — open it on another screen (for example, this page on a computer): a phone can’t scan its own screen.
gw_issue.qr.panel: Point your phone’s camera at the QR code below.
gw_issue.ros.copy_button: Copy the script with the “Copy” button below.
gw_issue.ros.done: Interfaces → {iface}: the “R” flag means connected; the network’s devices go through the VPN.
gw_issue.ros.import_file: Winbox or the web interface → Files: upload {script}, then New Terminal → /import file-name={script}
gw_issue.ros.net: If the router’s network isn’t 192.168.88.0/24 (the MikroTik default), replace it with yours in the script.
gw_issue.ros.paste_button: Winbox or the web interface → New Terminal → paste the script. A long one is easier as a file: {button} below, upload {script} to Files and run /import file-name={script}
gw_issue.ros.paste_menu: Winbox → New Terminal (in WebFig — Terminal) → paste the script. If it doesn’t copy in full (small window): “Save to files”, upload {script} to Files and run /import file-name={script}
gw_issue.send.bot: Forward the message with the link to yourself on {target} — for example, to Telegram “Saved Messages” — and copy it there.
gw_issue.send.default: Send it to yourself on {target} — for example, to Telegram “Saved Messages” — and copy it there.
gw_issue.send.page: Page open on another device? Send the link to yourself on {target} — for example, to Telegram “Saved Messages” — and copy it there.
gw_issue.steps.android_ikev2_add: In the VPN settings (Connections or Network & internet → VPN), add a profile: type IKEv2/IPSec MSCHAPv2; server address; IPsec identifier — the login; CA certificate — the installed one; server certificate — the one received from the server; username (the device login) and password.
gw_issue.steps.android_ikev2_ca: Certificate first: in the security settings (encryption and credentials), install a CA certificate — the file kaskad-ikev2-ca.crt.
gw_issue.steps.android_ikev2_note: Item names differ between manufacturers. There is also the strongSwan app: “IKEv2 EAP (Username/Password)”.
gw_issue.steps.asus_l2tp: VPN → VPN client (VPN Fusion) → “Add profile” → L2TP: {fields} → “Activate”.
gw_issue.steps.asus_l2tp_plain: The ASUS VPN client has no IPsec — it needs L2TP without encryption.
gw_issue.steps.asus_pptp: VPN → VPN client (VPN Fusion) → “Add profile” → PPTP: {fields} → “Activate”.
gw_issue.steps.huawei_l2tp: Advanced → VPN: turn VPN on, type L2TP.
gw_issue.steps.huawei_l2tp_fields: Server address (LNS) — the server’s address, username (the device login) and password; the IPsec key field, if there is one — the pre-shared key.
gw_issue.steps.huawei_l2tp_plain: Most Huawei 4G routers support L2TP only without IPsec.
gw_issue.steps.huawei_pptp: Advanced → VPN: turn VPN on, type PPTP; {fields}.
gw_issue.steps.ios_l2tp_add: Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → VPN → add a VPN configuration.
gw_issue.steps.ios_l2tp_fields: Type — L2TP; server — this server’s address; account — the login; password; secret — the PSK; “Send All Traffic” — on.
gw_issue.steps.keenetic_add: Internet → Other connections → VPN connections → “Create connection”.
gw_issue.steps.keenetic_l2tp: Type (protocol) — L2TP/IPsec; {fields}; “Secret key” — the IPsec pre-shared key (PSK).
gw_issue.steps.keenetic_save: Turn on “Use for accessing the Internet” and save.
gw_issue.steps.linux_ikev2: NetworkManager: package network-manager-strongswan → VPN → “IPsec/IKEv2 (strongswan)”: server, certificate — kaskad-ikev2-ca.crt, EAP authentication, login, password; “Request an inner IP address”.
gw_issue.steps.linux_l2tp: NetworkManager: package network-manager-l2tp-gnome → VPN → “L2TP”: gateway, login, password; “IPsec Settings” — enable, pre-shared key.
gw_issue.steps.linux_pptp: NetworkManager: package network-manager-pptp-gnome → VPN → “PPTP”: gateway, login, password; “Advanced” — MPPE encryption.
gw_issue.steps.linux_sstp: NetworkManager: package network-manager-sstp-gnome → VPN → “SSTP”: gateway address:port, login, password, CA certificate — the file kaskad-sstp.crt.
gw_issue.steps.macos_l2tp_add: System Settings → Network → the Action pop-up menu (…) → “Add VPN Configuration” → “L2TP over IPSec” (macOS 13: System Settings → VPN → “Add VPN Configuration”).
gw_issue.steps.macos_l2tp_fields: Server address, account name (login), password, Shared Secret; in options — send all traffic over the VPN.
gw_issue.steps.mikrotik: Winbox → New Terminal (in WebFig — Terminal) → paste the script (replace 192.168.88.0/24 with your network).
gw_issue.steps.tplink_check: First look for a “VPN client” section in the router menu (or the “L2TP” connection type under “Internet”): if there is neither, this router won’t work.
gw_issue.steps.tplink_l2tp_client: Has a “VPN client” (Archer and other new models): Advanced → VPN client → “Add”: L2TP/IPsec, {fields}, IPsec pre-shared key.
gw_issue.steps.tplink_l2tp_wan: No VPN client, but Network → Internet has the “L2TP” connection type (L2TP Russia): {fields}; secondary connection — “Dynamic IP”. Then the whole router goes through the VPN, and there is no IPsec there — {plain_on}.
gw_issue.steps.tplink_pptp_client: Has a “VPN client”: Advanced → VPN client → “Add”: PPTP, {fields}.
gw_issue.steps.tplink_pptp_wan: No VPN client, but Network → Internet has the “PPTP” connection type (PPTP Russia): {fields}; secondary connection — “Dynamic IP”.
gw_issue.steps.xiaomi_add: In the router’s web interface: advanced settings → VPN → add a service (names depend on the firmware).
gw_issue.steps.xiaomi_l2tp: Protocol L2TP; server — this server’s address, username (the device login) and password; turn on “Connect automatically”.
gw_issue.steps.xiaomi_l2tp_plain: Xiaomi routers support L2TP only without IPsec.
gw_issue.steps.xiaomi_pptp: In the router’s web interface: advanced settings → VPN → add a service: protocol PPTP, {fields} (names depend on the firmware).

gw_issue.win.connect: Settings → Network & internet → VPN → “{name}” → “Connect”. Windows asks for the login and password — they are below, in “Connection details”.
